topic: Acids, Bases, Salts, and pH Scale
description: Chemical compounds that dissolve in water to yield specific ions are classified as acids or bases. Their interaction produces salts, and the strength of their acidic or basic nature is measured using the pH scale.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: General definitions and physical properties of acids, bases, and salts.

key_concepts.explanation: Substances that are sour in taste, turn blue litmus paper red, and release hydrogen ions (H+) when dissolved in aqueous solutions.

Substances that are bitter in taste, soapy to touch, turn red litmus paper blue, and release hydroxide ions (OH-) in aqueous solutions. Bases that are soluble in water are specifically called alkalis.
Ionic compounds formed as a result of a neutralization reaction between an acid and a base.

sections.title: Scientific Theories
sections.description: Chemical theories that define the fundamental nature of acids and bases.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Acids are substances that produce H+ ions in water, and bases produce OH- ions in water.
scientific_principles.application: Used to explain the behavior of acids and bases in aqueous solutions.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Acids are proton (H+) donors, whereas bases are proton (H+) acceptors.
scientific_principles.application: Helps explain chemical reactions in both aqueous and non-aqueous solutions.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Acids are electron pair acceptors, and bases are electron pair donors.
scientific_principles.application: Crucial for understanding the formation of complex coordination compounds.
The mechanism behind using antacids (mild bases) to neutralize excess stomach acid.

sections.title: pH Scale and Indicators
sections.description: Tools and substances used to measure and visually detect the acidity or basicity of a solution.

key_concepts.explanation: Developed by S.P.L. Sørensen in 1909, it is the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration (pH = -log[H+]). The scale ranges from 0 to 14 (pH < 7 is acidic, pH = 7 is neutral, pH > 7 is basic).

key_associations.extra_info: Turns red in an acidic medium and blue in a basic medium.
Remains colorless in acidic solutions and turns pink in basic solutions.
Turns red in strongly acidic solutions and yellow in basic solutions.

sections.title: Important Facts and Daily Uses
sections.description: Crucial data points, pH values of common substances, and key chemical formulas.

important_facts.fact: The pH of normal human blood is approximately 7.4, making it slightly basic.
The pH of pure (distilled) water is exactly 7.0 at 25°C.
The human stomach secretes Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) with a pH of about 1.5 to 2.0 to aid in protein digestion.
Precipitation is officially classified as 'Acid Rain' when its pH level drops below 5.6.
Tooth decay accelerates when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5, which degrades the tooth enamel (calcium phosphate).
Aqua Regia is a highly corrosive 3:1 volumetric mixture of concentrated Hydrochloric acid (HCl) and concentrated Nitric acid (HNO3) capable of dissolving noble metals like gold and platinum.
The chemical name for Baking Soda is Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3).
The chemical name for Washing Soda is Sodium Carbonate Decahydrate (Na2CO3.10H2O).
